content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNDevOps

Deploys and promotions are the everyday use. Release cuts are the occasional one.

**Verify before you advise.** Every claim about this pipeline that was written down has been wrong
somewhere — `tagging.md` describes sprint tagging that is dead, `README.md:78` names the wrong MRT
target, Confluence carries three different promotion orders. `.research/DEVOPS-STATE.md` is a list
of things to re-check, **never a source of fact.** Derive state live, every time.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

---

## Modes

| Mode | Does |
|---|---|
| `status` *(default)* | Full state. A bare invocation stops here. |
| `deploy <env> <ref>` | Preflight, then dispatch on approval |
| `promote <from> <to>` | Takes what `<from>` is running and deploys it to `<to>` |
| `tag <version>` | Validates the name, checks the tag workflow is even present, cuts on approval |
| `release` | The full cut — changelog, tag, promote |
| `sync-env <env>` | `sync-env-vars-to-mrt.yml`. Prod is excluded by design. |
| `rollback <env>` | Either documented path, with the gap stated first |

**Two workflows are not dispatchable.** `deploy-dev.yml` fires only on push to `develop`.
`deploy-sit.yml` fires only on a successful `SIT Gate` `workflow_run`. If asked to deploy either,
say so and explain what actually triggers them — do not attempt a dispatch that will fail.

---

## Every invocation starts here

### 1. The ladder — what is each environment running?

```bash
for e in dev test sit uat staging prod; do
  gh api "repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=$e&per_page=1" \
    --jq 'if length==0 then "never deployed" else "\(.[0].ref) @ \(.[0].sha[:7]) — \(.[0].created_at[:10])" end'
done
```

Print all six with their age. **Flag staleness** — an environment weeks behind the one below it is
the context you would otherwise reconstruct by hand, and it changes whether a promotion is routine
or a leap.

### 2. Pipeline health

- **Environment protection rules** — `gh api repos/.../environments/<env>`. Report `protection_rules`
  and `deployment_branch_policy` honestly. As of the last check every environment returned `[]` and
  `null`, meaning no reviewer stands between a dispatch and that environment.
- **Can `SIT Gate` pass?** Does any `**/*.p0.spec.{js,ts}` exist · are `LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL`,
  `LHCI_TOKEN`, `LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT` present · is `RETAIL_APP_HOME` set anywhere the job can read.
  If not, `release/**` merges are blocked and `deploy-sit.yml` cannot fire.
- **Does the target environment have the vars this deploy needs?** `prod` has historically held
  none — its MRT vars are set by hand in the console.
- **Recent runs of the workflow about to fire** — `gh api .../workflows/<file>/runs`. A workflow
  with zero runs is about to execute for the first time. Say so.
- **Do the undeclared binaries still resolve?** `bundlesize`, `cross-env` and `@lhci/cli` are not in
  `package.json`; they arrive transitively through `@salesforce/retail-react-app`.

---

## Which ref may go where

| Tier | Accepts |
|---|---|
| `dev` | not dispatchable — auto on push to `develop` |
| `test` | a tag **or** a branch ref, for on-demand looks |
| `sit` | not dispatchable — `workflow_run` off `SIT Gate` |
| `uat`, `staging`, `prod` | **a `vX.Y.Z` tag** |

**Refuse a branch ref above `test`** unless explicitly overridden, and give the reason:
`versionGuard.mjs` skips any ref that is not a `v*` tag, so a branch ref means the downgrade guard
does not run — nothing prevents deploying something older than what is live.

Expect this to bite. **Every deployment to date has used `ref=develop`**, so the first tag-based
promotion will be the first time this rule has ever applied.

## Promotion order

`uat → staging → prod`, per `.claude/rules/tagging.md` as the Tier 1 source.

**Where a promotion also involves Contentful, say so:** `contentfulMapping.ts` and the Contentful
scripts promote content **staging before uat** — the opposite order. Both are internally consistent
and nothing explains the difference. Surface it and let Marcel decide; do not silently pick.

## The three namespaces

| Name | Where it is the truth |
|---|---|
| `prod` | GitHub Environment · `versionGuard` argument · `.env.prod` · `ENVIRONMENT_NAME` |
| `production` | `config/production.js` · `DEPLOY_TARGET` · **the MRT target** (`push:prod` → `-t production`) |
| `master` | the Contentful environment |

`README.md:78` tells a tier-1 approver to set production env vars in the MRT console under `prod`.
**The target is `production`.** Production is the one tier with no automated var sync, so this is
the only path — use the right name.

---

## Executing

Nothing runs without approval. Present, then wait.

For **irreversible** actions, print the literal command and state the consequence plainly before
asking:

- **Any tag** — *"This tag cannot be deleted or moved by anyone, including you. The `tag-rc` ruleset
  has zero bypass actors."*
- **A deploy to `prod`** — *"No environment reviewer exists. `versionGuard` will "* + (skip this ref
  / block a downgrade), whichever is true for the ref in hand.
- **Any first-ever run of a workflow** — *"`deploy-stg.yml` has never executed. This is its first run."*

Then dispatch:

```bash
gh workflow run deploy-<env>.yml -f ref=<ref>
```

Report the run URL, watch it to completion, and report the real outcome — not the dispatch's exit code.

## Tagging

Before cutting any tag:

1. **Validate the name** against both patterns — `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+-rc\.\d+$` and
   `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-hotfix\.\d+)?$`. Nothing else is accepted anywhere, and **no layer matches
   anything but lowercase `v*`** — `V0.1.0` or `0.1.0` slips past the hook, the workflow and both
   rulesets.
2. **Check `tag-validate.yml` exists on the branch being tagged.** GitHub evaluates a tag workflow
   from the tagged commit; the file has historically lived only on `develop`, so a tag cut from a
   release branch is not validated at all. Say which is true right now.
3. **Annotated only** — `git tag -a <tag> -m "<message>"`. Never lightweight. Never `npm version`;
   its commit is blocked by `release/**` protection.
4. **Push the tag alone** — `git push origin <tag>`.

## Rollback

Both paths, and state the gap before either:

> `rollback=true` skips the version downgrade guard, and no environment required reviewer exists to
> catch a mistake. Nothing else is watching this.

- **Controlled** — `gh workflow run deploy-<env>.yml -f ref=<previous-tag> -f rollback=true`
- **Emergency** — re-activate the previous MRT bundle by hand, then
  `node scripts/versionGuard.mjs record <env> <ref>` so the Deployment record matches reality

## Release cut

1. `/generate-changelog` — the team's skill, and `tagging.md` says run it before cutting
2. Cut `release/vX.Y.Z` from `develop`
3. RC tags as needed, each deployed to `test`
4. Merge to `main`, bump `package.json` (Tier 1 — needs an approver)
5. Final `vX.Y.Z` tag on the merge commit — tier-1-approvers only
6. Promote `uat → staging → prod`
7. Back-merge to `develop` — required by `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, enforced by nothing

Offer `/upstream-sync-review` when the upstream watcher has flagged a new base version.

---

## When a gate is broken

**Report it, name the owner, and stop.**

Do not work around it, do not fix it, do not draft the escalation. `.github/workflows/` and
environment configuration are **Tier 1**, owned by Integration / SI Partner, routed to
`@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` by `CODEOWNERS`. Not yours to change.

Give the evidence — the command, its real output, the file and line — so the report stands on its
own when Marcel takes it to whoever owns it.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never dispatch, tag, push or roll back without explicit approval.**
- **Never modify `.github/workflows/`, `config/`, `package.json`, `.claude/**` or any Tier 1 file.**
- **Never present cached state as current.** If you did not check it this run, say so.
- **Never claim a deploy succeeded from the dispatch's exit code.** Watch the run.
- **Never guess an MRT target name.** `production`, not `prod`.
- **Say what you could not verify** — MRT console state is not reachable from here, and that
  includes what production's env vars actually are.

## plugin:figma:figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests).
